name: Trichosurus vulpecula
plant_note: Eats leaves, flowers, buds and fruit, including roses, vegetables and fruit trees.
habitat: Tree hollows and roof spaces. A possum box in a tree gives it a home outside the house.
description: A grey or brown possum with large ears and a bushy black tail, active at night. It is protected.

name: Pseudocheirus peregrinus
plant_note: Eats leaves, flowers and fruit, including new rose shoots.
habitat: Dense shrubs and trees, where it builds a ball-shaped nest of leaves called a drey.
description: A small grey-brown possum with a white-tipped tail it curls around branches. It is protected.

name: Pteropus poliocephalus
plant_note: Feeds on nectar and pollen from gums and paperbarks and on fruit, carrying pollen and seeds over long distances.
habitat: Camps in tall trees, and flowering and fruiting trees for feeding.
hazard_note: Flying-foxes can carry Australian bat lyssavirus. Please do not touch one, even if it is hurt or tangled in netting; call a wildlife rescue group. If you are bitten or scratched, wash the wound with soap and water for 15 minutes and see a doctor straight away.
description: A large fruit bat with a grey head and a rusty collar. It is a threatened species.

name: Tachyglossus aculeatus
habitat: Leaf litter, logs and dense cover. Gaps under fences let it move between gardens.
description: A spiny, egg-laying mammal with a long snout that digs for ants and curls into a ball when disturbed.

name: Perameles nasuta
plant_note: Digs small cone-shaped holes in lawns for curl grubs and other insects.
habitat: Dense ground cover to shelter in, near lawns and leaf litter.
description: A small, grey-brown marsupial with a long pointed snout, active at night.

name: Vulpes vulpes
habitat: Bushland edges and suburbs, sheltering under houses and in dense weeds.
description: A reddish-brown fox with a white-tipped bushy tail, introduced in the 1850s. It hunts native wildlife and poultry.

name: Oryctolagus cuniculus
plant_note: Eats seedlings, vegetables and young plants down to the ground.
habitat: Warrens in open ground, and cover under shrubs and woodpiles.
description: A grey-brown rabbit, introduced in the 1850s, that damages gardens and bushland.

name: Rattus rattus
plant_note: Eats fruit, seeds and stored food.
habitat: Roof spaces, sheds, compost and dense vines.
description: A slender rat with a tail longer than its body, introduced from Europe. Native rats and marsupials can look similar.

name: Gambusia holbrooki
habitat: Still and slow water, including garden ponds and dams.

rules.text: Gambusia is a restricted noxious fish in Queensland. You must not keep it, feed it, give it away, sell it or release it into the environment. If you catch one, please kill it humanely and put it in the bin.

description: A small, dull olive fish brought in to control mosquitoes. It nips the fins of native fish and eats frog eggs and tadpoles.

name: Pseudomugil signifer
habitat: Ponds and streams with water plants. It is a good native fish for a garden pond.
description: A tiny native fish with bright blue eyes.

name: Cornu aspersum
plant_note: Eats seedlings, leafy vegetables and flowers at night. Please use iron-based bait or hand-pick it, as other baits can poison lizards, birds and pets.
habitat: Damp, shaded spots under pots, edging and dense plants.
description: A brown snail with a mottled, round shell, introduced from Europe.

name: Amanita muscaria
habitat: Under pines and birches, which it grows with.
hazard_note: It is poisonous. Please never eat a wild mushroom, and call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 if someone has.
description: A red mushroom with white flecks, brought to Australia with pine trees.

name: Aseroe rubra
description: A red, star-shaped fungus with a foul smell that draws flies to spread its spores. It breaks down mulch and is harmless to plants.

name: Trametes versicolor
description: A thin, banded bracket fungus that grows in overlapping tiers on dead wood and helps rot it down.

name: Leucocoprinus birnbaumii
habitat: Potting mix in pots and glasshouses.
hazard_note: It is poisonous to eat. Please keep it away from children and pets, and call the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 if someone has eaten it.
description: A small, bright yellow mushroom that pops up in potting mix. It does not harm the plant.
